s: Neural network models that convert text, images, or other data into dense vector representations for similarity search, clustering, and retrieval.
w: Embedding models transform input data into fixed-length numerical vectors where semantic similarity maps to geometric proximity. Text embedding models (e.g., OpenAI ada-002, Cohere embed, sentence-transformers) encode text into 768-3072 dimensional vectors. Models are served via dedicated inference endpoints with batching support for throughput. Vectors are stored in vector databases and retrieved via approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search. Model selection trades off quality, dimensionality, latency, and cost.
use: Similarity matching for recommendations and deduplication
Clustering and classification of unstructured text
avoid: Exact keyword matching scenarios where BM25 or TF-IDF are sufficient
Highly domain-specific text where general-purpose embeddings underperform
Real-time applications where embedding latency per query is unacceptable

props.batch_size: Number of texts encoded per inference call
props.model_variant: Specific model: small (fast/cheap) vs large (high quality)

size.embeddings_per_sec: ~100-1000 depending on model size and batch
size.vector_size_bytes: ~4-12 KB per vector depending on dimensions

pat.d: Embed documents asynchronously in large batches, store vectors in DB, serve queries with single-document embedding.
Use fast embedding model for candidate retrieval, then a cross-encoder reranker for precision on top-k results.

pits: Embedding drift when upgrading models without re-indexing existing vectors
Dimension mismatch between embedding model output and vector DB index configuration
Batch size too large causing OOM on embedding inference servers
Ignoring max token limits - truncation silently degrades embedding quality
tips: Measure embedding quality with domain-specific benchmarks, not just MTEB scores
Use dimensionality reduction (e.g., Matryoshka) to store compact vectors and improve retrieval speed
Cache embeddings for static content to avoid redundant inference calls
